title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative: In 2022, the Public Labor Prosecution Service (MPT) and Ministry of Labor and Employment (MTE) adopted the use of a spatial location methodology, called "Targeting Methodology", which increases its knowledge basis about labor violations, victims and perpetrators. Through the methodology, three target municipalities were chosen for a pilot initiative to combat child and slave labor. In March 2022, the Labor Secretariat of the then Ministry of Labor and Social Security launched the Brazilian Occupation Guide (GBO), which presents up-to-date information on the characteristics of occupations and the skills and behaviours required. The GBO is a tool that contributes, among others, to the formulation and implementation of public policies within the scope of the Public System of Employment, Work and Income in the context of the ILO Centenary Declaration for the Future of Work. In 2023, the Ministry of Labor and Employment expands the scope of the Brazilian Occupation Guide with the development of Occupational Projection Methodologies, which addresses the major ongoing trends that directly impact the future of work and the profile and demand of the most diverse occupations. In 2022, the Public Labor Prosecution Service (MPT) used Crisis Response Methodologies on two fronts: territorial scale and sectoral scale. In the first case, it was applied in The municipality of Minaçu, in the State of Goiás, applied a crisis response methodology, which is gradually undergoing a change in mineral exploration activity. In the sectoral aspect, the methodology was applied in the slaughterhouse sector of 42 municipalities in 9 federal units of the country. The results make it possible to identify vulnerable population groups, decent work deficits and opportunities to generate employment, work and income, in the context of the response to the COVID-19 pandemic crisis. A.Between 2022 and 2023, the ILO provided technical support to the Public Labor Prosecution Service (MPT) and the Labor Inspection Secretariat (SIT) of the Ministry of Labor and Employment (MTE) through the development of a spatial location methodology, called Targeting Methodology, applied to the coffee production chain in the State of Minas Gerais. B. Between 2020 and 2022, the ILO technically collaborated with the Secretariat of Labor, of the Ministry of Labor and Employment (MTE), in the design and development of the Brazilian Occupation Guide (GBO), which presents updated information on the characteristics of occupations and the skills and behaviors required. C. In 2023, the ILO contributed technically with the Secretariat of Labor, of the Ministry of Labor and Employment (MTE), in the development of Occupational Projection Methodologies for Brazil, addressing the major ongoing trends that directly impact the future of work and the profile and demand of the most diverse occupations. D. Between 2020 and 2022, the ILO technically collaborated with the Public Labor Prosecution Service (MPT) in the development of Methodologies for Responses to the Covid-19 Crisis, applied on a territorial and sectoral scale.

Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: With the labour reform enacted in Brazil in 2017, labour unions experienced a significant reduction in their available resources. Consequently, their capacity to contribute and actively participate in tripartite dialogues diminished, creating an imbalance of power in the tripartite process of revising Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) standards initiated by the government in 2019. Fortunately, through a grant provided by the ILO office in Brazil, workers were capacitated and gained the ability to engage more effectively in the revision of standards and collaborative working groups. This support allowed them to access specialist guidance and conduct in-depth studies related to specific standards, such as NR 01, NR 03, NR 17, and NR 31, as well as the implementation of the Risk Management Program. Additionally, they were able to contribute actively to the working groups for the National Policy for Occupational Health and Safety, including the group addressing psychosocial risks. With this invaluable support, the tripartite revision process for these standards and policies was carried out within a more balanced and inclusive environment. Accordingly, the overall social dialogue process on OSH policies was enhanced and became more effective and inclusive. Between 2021 and 2022, with RBSA support, Central Unica dos Trabalhadores (CUT) strengthened its capacities to participate in the elaboration and revision of the National OSH Standards and Regulations (NRs) in the Permanent Tripartite Parity Committee (CTPP). To this end, the ILO provided support to: a) Technical support to the Workers' Bench in the Tripartite Study Group on psychosocial risks with the preparation of technical material and support to the Workers' Bench in the 4 meetings on Study Group contributing to the debate and appropriation of the theme; b) Technical support at the meeting with representatives of the union centrals for the organization of the National Seminar of the Centrals on Psychosocial Risks; c) Technical support for the planning, organization and realization of the National Seminar of the Trade Union Centers on Psychosocial Risks; d) Technical study of the National Worker's Health and Safety Policy, which aimed to support the workers' bench during their intervention in the meetings of the Tripartite Working Group on the National Worker's Health and Safety Policy, as well as a qualified participation in the discussions carried out on the subject in the CTPP; e) The holding of two seminars on “Health, Work and the Environment” with Union Leaders, Health Secretaries of the state CUTs and Branches and CUT representatives in the Tripartite Commission on Health and Safety at Work (CT-SST), as well as partners who were involved in its preparation and publication, research on the topic and analysis of the text of the policy in force. The seminars held had the objective of contributing to the rescue of the process of elaboration of the National Policy on Health and Safety at Work, in addition to contributing to thinking about its expansion and strengthening of the dialogue on the subject.
